edition: Silent Hill: Book of Memories, PS Vita (2012)
sourceCredit: Martial Duchemin, PSVitaGen, 23 October 2012. Photographs of in-game rendering in this article are direct gameplay screen captures. Source article describes this encounter and its smaller summoned creatures.
retrieval: The original article links twenty public small JPEGs and corresponding full-size asset filenames. The current global asset host yielded empty bodies for the full-size links. The linked media origin still served the named full-size assets (HTTP 200). Four full-size 960×544 screenshots retained, without digital enlargement or colour adjustment.
result: First selection and lateral combat candidate justified for the mobile phase. See the final import journal for outcomes.

evidence.observation: Rooted phase, source cutscene. Close-up of paired raised wooden shoulders, hollow pointed hood and ribbed trunk. Lower windings and background branches are occluded in this shot.

Uprooted boss, central and larger than the four surrounding Wood Saplings. The forked twigs of its shoulder and pointed lower tips all fit in the frame against the ground. The player stands separately at bottom centre.

Mobile phase, lateral bent posture in an action from the encounter. Shows the side planes of the hood and rounded angular shoulder, long jointed forearm and the curved twig fingers of the far arm. Opposite arm exits the image on the left.

Uprooted mobile boss from a three-quarter angle with two arms in different poses, shoulder forks, bark ridge, hooked narrow leg and sharply tapered root ends. Entire visible outline fits the unobstructed ground below the interface. The player is separate at lower right.

limits: Native source game uses an oblique camera, polygonal detail and directional shading. Rear-facing detail, underside and fine branching behind the shoulder remain uncertain.
Character dimensions and boss scale are corroborated against four of its Wood Saplings in image 16. The smaller surrounding units and scenery are distinct.
The angled combat pose interprets the mobile posture across images 19 and 20. A complete perpendicular turntable or 1:1 model match is unavailable.
